purpose: Preserve the usefulness of weak, provisional, unverified, stale, external, heuristic, reputational, model-derived, or otherwise non-authoritative signals without allowing them to masquerade as authority-critical proof.
principle: Evidence quality is contextual. A signal can be useful without being sufficient for identity, authorization, execution, legal, or external-truth claims.

must_not_do: convert absence of proof into proof

may_influence: whether a consequential effect is admitted
must_not_do: claim more than its scope, purpose, destination, budget, audience or expiry
prove arbitrary external truth without an appropriate witness or oracle

promotion_rule: Moving evidence from advisory/corroborative use into a required proof position requires an explicit verifier, trust policy, freshness rule, scope binding, and failure mode. Promotion is never implicit.
demotion_rule: Evidence that is stale, unverifiable, revoked, ambiguous, context-shifted, or outside its intended scope may remain useful as advisory context but loses authority-critical standing.
positive_uses: Use DNS/AID/DID/repository or community metadata to find candidate endpoints or identities before stronger checks.
Use model or reputation signals to prioritize review, not to grant permission.
Use stale-but-benign metadata as a hint for recovery or investigation while refusing it at the effect boundary.
Use external claims to form hypotheses and select tests without treating those claims as established facts.
Use partial continuity evidence to reconnect user experience while requiring stronger proof before privileged recovery.
anti_patterns: treating advisory confidence as authorization confidence
letting reputation or popularity satisfy proof requirements
using stale verified state to override fresher denial or revocation
requiring expensive verification for low-consequence advisory uses where no protected effect depends on it
